cards.title: Introduction to Blueprints
cards.content:
In Flask, a Blueprint is an object that allows you to record operations to be applied to an application when it is loaded.

Blueprints make it easy to structure large applications into distinct components and reusable modules.

options.text: To replace HTML templates in Flask
To organize large applications into modular components
To connect directly to SQL databases

cards.title: Creating a Blueprint
cards.content:
To create a blueprint, you import the Blueprint class and instantiate it, typically in a dedicated module file.

from flask import Blueprint

auth_bp = Blueprint('auth', __name__, url_prefix='/auth')

@auth_bp.route('/login')
def login():
    return 'Login Page'

cards.title: Registering a Blueprint
cards.content:
Once a blueprint is defined, it must be registered with your main Flask application using the app.register_blueprint() method.

from flask import Flask
from auth import auth_bp

app = Flask(__name__)
app.register_blueprint(auth_bp)

cards.title: Advanced Blueprint Features
cards.content:
Blueprints can also have their own static files and templates. When you specify a template_folder, Flask will check the blueprint's template folder if it cannot find the template in the main application's template directory.

admin_bp = Blueprint('admin', __name__, template_folder='templates')
